edges.description: Without cytochrome b the complex III holoenzyme cannot be built, and its nuclear-encoded subunits are destabilized.
Assembled complex III is needed for respiratory supercomplexes, so its loss also reduces complex I.
Without assembled complex III, electron transfer from ubiquinol to cytochrome c fails.
The secondary complex I reduction adds to the electron transport defect.
Failure of oxidative phosphorylation diverts pyruvate to lactate, producing the severe and persistent lactic acidosis seen in both patients.
The proximal tubule is highly dependent on oxidative metabolism; tubulopathy is shared with other complex III assembly defects such as BCS1L deficiency.
Both patients had seizures; the energy failure in the brain is the presumed link, with no direct study of neuronal mechanism in this disease.
Both patients were growth-restricted before birth, suggesting the energy defect is already limiting in fetal life; the intermediate steps are unknown.
The surviving patient had severe developmental delay with absent speech; a neurological consequence of the energy defect is presumed but not shown.
In the second patient, seizures progressed to status epilepticus.

nodes.description: UQCC2 and UQCC1 are the human orthologs of the yeast cytochrome b assembly factors Cbp6p and Cbp3p. They interact, each needs the other to be stable, and together with the membrane anchor C16orf91 they form the COMA complex that facilitates translation of cytochrome b. In UQCC2-deficient cells the complex is absent.

nodes.description: Biallelic UQCC2 variants remove almost all functional UQCC2. The splice-site allele c.214-3C>G uses cryptic acceptor sites and leaves about 2% of wild-type transcript, with no stable aberrant protein; the homozygous p.[Arg8Pro;Leu10Phe] allele causes near-complete loss of UQCC2 protein in muscle and fibroblasts. Lentiviral re-expression of UQCC2 in patient fibroblasts corrects the complex III defect, which establishes causality. No catalytic activity is known for UQCC2; the only molecular activity shown for it is binding to UQCC1, which is why the molecular function bound here is the broad protein binding term rather than anything more specific.
